_comment: System and Communications Protection Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; pairs with SI (SC-7 boundary alarms feed SI-4 monitoring), AU (SC-8 / SC-13 cryptographic events go into the audit trail), IA (SC-12 key establishment underwrites IA-5 authenticators), and CM (SC-7 boundary changes route through CM-3 change control). Largest technical family in 800-53 r5 — 51 base controls authored at moderate baseline scope.
title: System and Communications Protection Plan
description: Documents how the system protects information at rest and in transit, partitions trust, defends boundaries, manages cryptographic key material, secures DNS / certificate / session integrity, and provides architectural protections (process isolation, DoS resilience, mobile-code containment). Covers the controls of the SC family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-52 r2 (TLS), NIST SP 800-57 (Key Management), NIST SP 800-77 r1 (IPsec VPNs), NIST SP 800-95 (Web Services Security), FIPS 140-3 (Cryptographic Module Validation), and FIPS 199 / FIPS 200.
intro_template:
This System and Communications Protection Plan documents the protections applied to {system_name}'s communications channels, cryptographic operations, network boundary, and shared system resources. It establishes the practices, tooling, cadences, and roles used to safeguard data in transit and at rest, manage cryptographic key material across its lifecycle, partition trusted from untrusted code, secure name resolution, defend against denial-of-service, and contain mobile code.

The scope covers boundary protection, transmission protection, cryptographic key establishment and management, FIPS-validated cryptographic protection, data at rest, secure name resolution (authoritative and recursive), session authenticity, mobile-code controls, process isolation, and resource-availability protections within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (System and Communications Protection family), NIST SP 800-52 r2 (TLS), NIST SP 800-57 (Key Management), and FIPS 140-3 (Cryptographic Module Validation Program).
approach_template:
{system_name} relies on {boundary_tooling} for boundary protection, {encryption_in_transit_tooling} for protection of data in transit, {encryption_at_rest_tooling} for protection of data at rest, and {key_management_system} for cryptographic key management. FIPS 140-3 validation status of cryptographic modules is tracked at {fips_validation_evidence}. DNS integrity is protected via {dns_protection_summary}.

Additional details on boundary protection, transmission protection, cryptographic key management, FIPS-validated protection, data at rest, name resolution, session authenticity, mobile code, and architectural protections are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Communications-protection performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (TLS coverage rate, certificate-expiration lead time, FIPS-validated module coverage, boundary alarm volume + signal-to-noise, DNSSEC validation rate, key-rotation SLA compliance). The cryptographic inventory is reviewed on the cadence in §6.2; certificate expirations are managed via the automation described in §4.4 with alerts well in advance of expiration. Boundary alarms (SC-7(18) fail-secure events, SC-7 unauthorized connection attempts) feed the SI-4 monitoring pipeline and the IR triage queue.
integration_template: This System and Communications Protection Plan does not stand alone. The CM family deploys boundary and cryptographic configuration changes through the change-control workflow; the SI family monitors boundary alarms and integrity events; the AU family captures cryptographic-key-management and boundary-incident events; the IA family relies on SC-12 key establishment to underwrite authenticators; the CP family inherits cryptographic-recovery requirements when restoring from backup. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where SC-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

commonly_inheritable_controls.from: Enterprise PKI / CA infrastructure (when shared certificate authority underwrites system certs)
Enterprise FIPS-validated cryptographic module library / provider
Enterprise authoritative DNS service (when externally hosted with DNSSEC)
Enterprise DNS service architecture (internal + external authoritative split)

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Tooling and one-line summaries that anchor the rest of the plan.

questions.label: Boundary protection tooling (one-liner)
questions.help: Primary boundary defense (e.g., 'Palo Alto NGFW + AWS Network Firewall + AWS WAF', 'Cisco Firepower + ACI segmentation', 'Azure Firewall Premium + App Gateway WAF').

questions.label: Encryption in transit (one-liner)
questions.help: TLS terminator(s) + version policy (e.g., 'TLS 1.3 enforced at AWS ALB; TLS 1.2 minimum on internal mTLS via Istio').

questions.label: Encryption at rest (one-liner)
questions.help: Mechanisms protecting data at rest (e.g., 'AWS KMS-managed CMKs for EBS / S3 / RDS; LUKS for on-prem; SQL TDE for legacy DB').

questions.label: Key management system (one-liner)
questions.help: Cryptographic key custody (e.g., 'AWS KMS (FIPS 140-2 L3 HSM-backed) for app data; HashiCorp Vault for secrets; internal CA for mTLS certificates').

questions.label: FIPS 140-3 validation evidence location
questions.help: Where FIPS 140-3 / 140-2 validation certificates are tracked (e.g., 'Cryptographic-inventory register in GRC tool; vendor CMVP certs filed at /repo/compliance/crypto/').

questions.label: DNS protection summary (one-liner)
questions.help: Brief phrase summarizing DNS integrity / DNSSEC / DoH posture. Detail goes in the Name Resolution sub-section.

family_questions.label: Boundary Protection (SC-7)
family_questions.description: Network boundary architecture, ingress / egress controls, and managed interfaces.

questions.label: Boundary topology summary
questions.help: Where the authorization boundary sits relative to the internet, partner networks, and other systems. DMZ structure, public subnets, private subnets, transit gateway, etc. Reference an architecture diagram if maintained.

questions.label: Default-deny enforcement
options: Default deny on ingress and egress (SC-7(5) full)
Default deny ingress, monitored egress (SC-7(5) ingress only)
Stateful inspection without strict default deny

questions.label: Egress filtering approach (SC-7(4) / SC-7(5))
questions.help: How outbound traffic is restricted: allowlisted destinations, DNS-based egress filtering (e.g., AWS Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall), proxy-enforced URL category filtering, SNI inspection.

questions.label: Split-tunneling restriction (SC-7(7))
options: Split-tunneling allowed only for specific allowlisted destinations
Not applicable (no remote access tunnels in this system)

questions.label: External telecom routing (SC-7(8))
questions.help: How traffic to external organizations or networks is routed through proxies / gateways for inspection. Reference any TIC / TIC 3.0 alignment for federal systems.

questions.label: Boundary-rule change review
questions.help: Cadence at which boundary-policy / firewall-rule sets are reviewed for stale or overly permissive rules (e.g., 'Quarterly NIPR review; immediate review on any expedited add').

family_questions.label: Transmission Protection (SC-8)
family_questions.description: TLS / mTLS / IPsec coverage, version policy, and inspection.

questions.label: Internal traffic TLS posture
options: mTLS enforced on all internal east-west traffic (zero trust)
TLS enforced on all internal traffic (one-way auth)
TLS enforced for service-to-service; cleartext only on isolated control plane

questions.label: Cipher / curve policy
questions.help: Approved ciphers and elliptic curves (e.g., 'TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256; ECDH curves P-256 / P-384'). Reference NIST SP 800-52 r2.

questions.label: TLS inspection / break-and-inspect
questions.help: Whether and how outbound TLS is inspected for malware / DLP. Boundary location of break-and-inspect; PKI trust establishment on endpoints; bypass list for sensitive destinations (banking, healthcare).

questions.label: Legacy cleartext traffic register
questions.help: Any cleartext flows that remain (e.g., legacy SCADA, isolated test net). Compensating controls and POA&M reference.

family_questions.label: Cryptographic Key Establishment & Management (SC-12)
family_questions.description: Key lifecycle: generation, distribution, storage, rotation, destruction.

questions.label: Key generation method
options: Mixed (HSM for high-assurance keys; software module otherwise)

questions.label: Key storage protection
questions.help: How key material is protected at rest. HSM-backed, sealed by KMS, escrow process. Reference NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 §6 for storage requirements.

questions.label: Rotation policy by key class
questions.help: Rotation frequency by key class. Example: 'Customer master keys: annual; data encryption keys: per-object; signing keys: 2 years (overlapping); session keys: per-session; TLS certificates: 90 days (Let's Encrypt) / 1 year (internal CA).'

questions.label: Key compromise recovery procedure
questions.help: Steps when a key is suspected compromised. Revocation of dependent certs, rotation of dependent secrets, notification to stakeholders. Reference IR plan for incident handling.

questions.label: Key destruction method
questions.help: How keys are destroyed at end of life. Cryptographic erasure for cloud KMS, zeroize commands for HSM, NIST SP 800-88 r1 sanitization for media holding key material.

questions.label: Cryptographic key inventory location
questions.help: Where the cryptographic-key inventory is maintained (CMDB, GRC tool, dedicated KMS dashboard). Reference SC-13 cryptographic inventory.

questions.label: Cryptographic module inventory summary
questions.help: List of cryptographic modules in use with FIPS 140-3 / 140-2 certificate numbers. Example: 'OpenSSL FIPS 3.0 (CMVP #4282) for app TLS; AWS KMS HSM (CMVP #4523) for key custody; macOS CoreCrypto (CMVP #4244) for endpoint encryption.'

questions.label: Use contexts requiring FIPS validation
options: Encryption at rest (filesystem, database, object storage)

questions.label: Re-accreditation tracking
questions.help: How FIPS certificate expiration is tracked and re-validated modules are adopted before expiry. Lead time, owner role.

family_questions.label: Data at Rest (SC-28)
family_questions.description: Encryption coverage by storage class and what's not yet protected.

questions.label: Envelope-encryption strategy
questions.help: How DEKs and KEKs are layered. Per-object DEKs, per-tenant DEKs, per-database DEKs. KEK rotation independent of DEK rotation. Reference NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 §5 envelope encryption.

questions.label: Classified / sensitive data handling
questions.help: If CUI / PII / classified data is in scope: special handling (separate keys, FIPS 140-3 L3, hardware-backed). Reference SI-12 for retention.

questions.label: Unprotected-data register (if any)
questions.help: Any locations where encryption at rest is not yet applied. Compensating controls (physical security, network isolation) and POA&M reference.

family_questions.label: Name Resolution Security (SC-20, SC-21, SC-22)
family_questions.description: DNSSEC, DNS forwarding, and DNS architecture.

questions.label: Authoritative DNS provider
questions.help: Who hosts the authoritative zones for system domains (e.g., 'AWS Route 53', 'Cloudflare DNS', 'enterprise BIND clusters').

questions.label: DNSSEC signing status (SC-20)
options: DNSSEC signed on all authoritative zones
DNSSEC signed on external zones only
DNSSEC signed on critical zones only (with rationale)
Not signed (with compensating controls and POA&M)

questions.label: Recursive / caching DNS provider (SC-21)
questions.help: Resolver(s) used by hosts (e.g., 'AWS Route 53 Resolver with DNS Firewall', 'Cisco Umbrella', 'Quad9 with DoT').

questions.label: DNSSEC validation enforcement (SC-21)
options: Validating resolvers (DNSSEC validation enforced on lookup)

questions.label: Internal / external DNS separation (SC-22)
questions.help: How internal and external DNS views are separated. Split-horizon DNS, internal-only zones, exfiltration-resistance via DNS firewall.

questions.label: DoH / DoT policy
questions.help: Whether DNS-over-HTTPS or DNS-over-TLS is enforced or restricted. Some orgs block external DoH to retain DNS-firewall visibility.

family_questions.label: Session Authenticity & Network Disconnect (SC-10, SC-15, SC-23)
family_questions.description: Session integrity, idle disconnect, and collaborative-computing controls.

questions.label: Session integrity mechanism (SC-23)
questions.help: How session authenticity is preserved (signed JWTs, session-bound tokens, mTLS-enforced bindings, Token Binding). Anti-replay, session-fixation prevention.

questions.label: Idle disconnect threshold (SC-10)
questions.help: Time after which an idle session is terminated. SC-10 ODV (e.g., '15 minutes for privileged sessions; 30 minutes for standard').

questions.label: Maximum total session lifetime
questions.help: Hard cap on session duration regardless of activity (e.g., '8 hours for users; 1 hour for service-to-service tokens').

questions.label: Collaborative-computing controls (SC-15)
questions.help: Camera / microphone / screen-share controls. Whether SC-15 ODV requires explicit indication when active. Common with VTC, Teams / Zoom integrations.

questions.label: Session revocation mechanism
questions.help: How sessions can be invalidated globally (compromise scenario): token-version increment, denylist cache, force-logout, OAuth refresh-token revocation.

family_questions.label: Mobile Code (SC-18)
family_questions.description: Restrictions on JavaScript / WASM / mobile applets / browser extensions.

questions.label: Authorized mobile-code list
questions.help: What mobile code is authorized to run in the system, by source / origin / trust level. Allowlist sources.

questions.label: Content Security Policy (CSP) posture
questions.help: If browser-facing: CSP policy summary. Strict-source vs nonce/hash, frame-ancestors, blocking inline scripts. Reference OWASP guidance.

questions.label: Office macro policy
options: Office macros disabled by GPO (allowlist signed only)

family_questions.label: Architectural Protections (SC-2, SC-3, SC-4, SC-39)
family_questions.description: Process isolation, separation of system and user functionality.

questions.label: User vs admin function separation (SC-2)
questions.help: How user and admin functionality are separated (different ports, different hosts, different identity domains, different management VLAN).

questions.label: Security-function isolation (SC-3)
questions.help: How security-relevant functions are isolated from non-security functions. Privilege rings, hypervisor / container boundaries, separate management plane.

questions.label: Shared-resource handling (SC-4)
questions.help: How information in shared system resources (memory, scratch disk, cache) is prevented from leaking between users / processes. Object reuse, memory-zeroing, cache partitioning.

questions.label: DoS mitigation mechanisms
options: DDoS-protection service (AWS Shield / Cloudflare / Azure DDoS Protection)

questions.label: DoS runbook reference
questions.help: Pointer to the DoS-response runbook in the IR plan / wiki. Activation criteria, escalation path.

family_questions.label: Protection Scope and Coverage
family_questions.description: Quantitative scope numbers that anchor metrics later in the plan.

questions.label: Endpoints / services with TLS requirement
questions.help: Approximate count of services that must serve TLS (informs TLS coverage rate in metrics).

questions.label: Active certificate count
questions.help: Approximate count of active TLS / signing certificates managed by the system.

questions.label: Data-at-rest volume (approximate)
questions.help: Total volume of data at rest under encryption (e.g., '50 TB across S3 + RDS + EFS').

questions.label: Managed-interface count at boundary
questions.help: Approximate count of managed interfaces at the authorization boundary (informs SC-7(3) summary).

family_questions.label: Communications-Protection Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate SC control effectiveness.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: TLS coverage rate (% of services serving TLS minimum version)
Certificate-expiration lead time (mean days from alert to renewal)
FIPS-validated module coverage (% of crypto operations on validated modules)
Key-rotation SLA compliance (% rotated within policy)
Encryption-at-rest coverage rate (% of storage volume encrypted)
Open POA&M items linked to SC controls

family_questions.label: Boundary Coverage Verification
family_questions.description: How the org continuously verifies SC boundary tooling is correctly deployed.

questions.label: Boundary-inventory reconciliation cadence
questions.help: How often the documented boundary diagram is reconciled with actual deployed firewalls / SGs / WAFs.

questions.label: Boundary-rule review cadence
questions.help: How often firewall rule sets are reviewed for stale, overly permissive, or deprecated rules.

questions.label: Certificate-inventory reconciliation cadence
questions.help: How often certificate inventory is reconciled (CT logs, ACM, internal CA exports). Detects shadow / orphan certs.

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the SC control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.13').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for SC findings
questions.help: Convention for SC-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-SC-' for general; 'POAM-SC7-' for boundary findings).

questions.label: CM change-workflow integration
questions.help: How boundary / TLS / cryptographic configuration changes route through CM-3 change control. Emergency-bypass for incident response.

questions.label: SI-4 monitoring handoff
questions.help: How SC-7 boundary alarms (denied connections, fail-secure events, anomalous flows) feed the SI-4 monitoring pipeline.

questions.label: AU event handoff
questions.help: How cryptographic-key-management events, certificate-issuance events, and boundary-incident events flow into the audit pipeline.

questions.label: IA-5 authenticator dependency
questions.help: Where IA-5 authenticator material relies on SC-12 key establishment (PIV cert issuance, FIDO-key attestation, mTLS service identity).

questions.label: CP recovery dependency
questions.help: Where CP recovery procedures depend on SC key material (KMS keys must be available for backup decryption; HSM partition restoration during DR).

questions.label: CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy reference
questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document tying SC continuous-monitoring metrics to the broader ConMon plan.

glossary.definition: Per SC-7, controls that monitor and protect communications at the system boundary. Includes firewalls, gateways, proxies, and managed interfaces.
The set of hardware, software, and / or firmware that implements cryptographic functions and is the unit of FIPS 140-3 / 140-2 validation.
Data Encryption Key (encrypts user data) and Key Encryption Key (encrypts DEKs). Standard layering in envelope encryption per NIST SP 800-57.
DNS Security Extensions — cryptographic signing of DNS records to provide origin authenticity and integrity. Required for SC-20 authoritative-zone signing on federal systems.
Encrypting data with a DEK and then encrypting the DEK with a KEK. Allows DEK rotation per object without re-encrypting the underlying data.
Per SC-7(18), the property that a boundary device denies traffic by default when it fails or its configuration is unavailable. Contrast with fail-open.
Federal Information Processing Standard 140-3 — validation requirements for cryptographic modules. Successor to FIPS 140-2.
Hardware Security Module — a physical device designed for cryptographic key storage and processing, typically FIPS 140-3 / 140-2 Level 3 validated.
Key Management System — infrastructure for generating, storing, distributing, rotating, and destroying cryptographic keys.
Per SC-7(3), a connection between the system and another system or network that has documented protections and is monitored.
Per SC-18, executable code that is transferred from a remote system to a target system (e.g., JavaScript, WebAssembly, Office macros, Java applets).
Mutual TLS — TLS where both client and server present certificates to authenticate each other. Common in service-to-service communication.
Perfect Forward Secrecy — a property of TLS cipher suites (ECDHE / DHE) where compromise of long-term keys does not compromise past session keys.
Public Key Infrastructure — the framework of certificate authorities, registration authorities, and certificates that supports asymmetric cryptography.
Per SC-39, separation of system processes such that one cannot read or write the memory or resources of another. Enforced via OS-level protections, hypervisors, containers, or hardware.
A DNS server that performs the recursive lookup process on behalf of clients (querying authoritative servers and returning the result). Subject to SC-21.
Per SC-23, assurance that the session is genuine (not hijacked, replayed, or fabricated). Enforced via session integrity mechanisms (signed tokens, mTLS, anti-replay).
A remote-access configuration where some traffic flows through the corporate VPN and other traffic flows directly to the internet. Restricted by SC-7(7) on most federal systems.
A DoS-mitigation technique where malicious connections are deliberately slowed or held to consume the attacker's resources rather than the target's.
Trusted Internet Connections 3.0 — federal initiative governing how agency networks connect to the internet. Influences SC-7(8) external-telecom routing.
Transport Layer Security — the cryptographic protocol securing data in transit. Required at SC-8 with NIST SP 800-52 r2 specifying acceptable versions and ciphers.
Web Application Firewall — a filter applied to HTTP / HTTPS traffic that detects and blocks application-layer attacks. Common at managed interfaces (SC-7) and feeds boundary alarms.
An architectural philosophy of 'never trust, always verify' — treating every request as untrusted regardless of source location. Drives mTLS-everywhere designs (SC-8 internal posture).
